land.text: the Dniester lands of the LBK's eastern extension

predecessors.note: The LBK infobox lists the Cucuteni-Trypillian culture among its successors and its eastern extension "leaped to the valley of the Dniester"; the Cucuteni page itself names roots in "the Starčevo-Körös-Criș and Vinča cultures of the 6th to 5th millennia" and the "Bug-Dniester culture (6500-5000 BC)".

correction.text: "from the Carpathian Mountains to the Dniester", "concentrated mainly in the Siret, Prut and Dniester river valleys": north-eastern Romania, Moldova and the Dniester lands of western Ukraine

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the early culture. Infobox "(c. 4800 to 3000 BC)", lead "(c. 5050 to 2950 BC)"; the chart's Early period (Pre-Cucuteni I-III to Cucuteni A-B, Trypillia A to BI-II) "5800 to 5000 BC" and "Cucuteni A phase seems to be very long (4600-4050)". The area drawn is about 160,000 km2 of the page's 350,000 km2 total, which the middle keyframe reaches.

correction.text: the full extent "from the Carpathian Mountains to the Dniester and Dnieper regions", "encompassing an area of 350,000 km2 (140,000 sq mi)"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the middle and late culture with the Southern Bug and Dnieper mega-sites; the text's middle phase "c. 4100 to 3500 BC", mega-sites "possibly inhabited by 20,000 to 46,000 people" in the "5th millennium BC", Maidanetske c. 3700 BC. The gazetteer total of these units is about 265,000 km2 against the page's 350,000 km2 (ratio 0.76). The Late period (3500-3000 BC, Horodiștea-Foltești, Trypillia CII) keeps the shape because the page does not describe a contraction.

region.text: "from the Carpathian Mountains to the Dniester", "concentrated mainly in the Siret, Prut and Dniester river valleys": north-eastern Romania, Moldova and the Dniester lands of western Ukraine

ledger.note: 4800 BCE: the painted-pottery villages of Cucuteni-Trypillia rise between the Carpathians and the Dniester. Infobox "c. 4800 to 3000 BC"; the culture is "centered on modern-day Moldova" and covers "substantial parts of western Ukraine and northeastern Romania". The counterpart is the LBK, whose page claims the Dniester and lists this culture as a successor; the Cucuteni page names Starcevo-Koros-Cris, Vinča and Bug-Dniester roots instead, hence the low confidence.

region.text: "the basins and plains of the Dnieper and Southern Bug rivers of central Ukraine", with the mega-sites Talianki ("a population of 15,000 and covering an area of 335" ha) and Maidanetske

ledger.note: 4100 BCE: the middle phase and the mega-sites of the Southern Bug and Dnieper. The middle phase runs "c. 4100 to 3500 BC"; settlements grew into mega-sites "possibly inhabited by 20,000 to 46,000 people" in the 5th millennium BC, Talianki with "a population of 15,000 and covering an area of 335" hectares.
3500 BCE: the Late period (Horodiștea-Foltești, Trypillia CII), "3500 to 3000 BC" in the page's chart.

ledger.note: 3000 BCE: the culture ends under the Kurgan expansion. Infobox end 3000 BC; "during the third wave of Kurgan expansion between 3000-2800 BC"; Mallory's ranges "Cucuteni-Trypillia (4800-2750 BC) and the Yamnaya culture (3300-2600 BC)"; a Sub-Boreal drought "Beginning around 3200 BC". The Yamnaya has no dossier yet.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture drawn by modern units: the Carpathian edge is firm, the steppe edge toward the Dnieper and the Black Sea is soft.

sources.title: Cucuteni–Trypillia culture
sources.note: Dates (4800-3000 / 5050-2950 BC), the three periods, the rivers and countries, the 350,000 km2 area, the mega-sites, the Kurgan end.

notes: Culture dossier, one page; the culture outlives the group's 3400 BCE horizon and is drawn to 3000 BCE so Moldova and western Ukraine are never blank. Disagreements: start 4800 (infobox) vs 5050 (lead) vs 5800 (chart) BC; end 3000 vs 2950 vs 2750 BC; the middle phase 5000-3500 (chart) vs 4100-3500 (text). Area check: 265,000 km2 drawn vs 350,000 km2 on the page. Usatovo is not on the page. The Yamnaya culture (3300-2600 BC) is a counterpart that needs a dossier (steppe, after this group's horizon). Gazetteer: Talianki, Maidanetske, Nebelivka, Cucuteni are not places; modern units stand in.
